ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AD \parallel BC$, $\angle B = 70^\circ$, $\angle C = 40^\circ$, $DE \parallel AB$ intersects $BC$ at point $E$. If $AD = 5\,cm$, $BC = 17\,cm$, then how many $cm$ is $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD\parallel BC$, $DE\parallel AB$,\\
therefore, quadrilateral ABED is a parallelogram,\\
thus, BE=AD=5,\\
therefore, EC=BC-BE=17cm-5cm=12cm,\\
since $DE\parallel AB$,\\
we have $\angle DEC=\angle B=70^\circ$,\\
given that $\angle C=40^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle EDC=180^\circ-\angle DEC-\angle C=70^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle EDC=\angle DEC$,\\
thus, CD=CE=\boxed{12cm}.
